excerpt: Maximum medical improvement means your condition has stabilised, not that you are healed. Why MMI is the turning point in an injury claim.
keyTakeaways: Maximum medical improvement (MMI) is when your condition stabilizes — not when you are fully healed. In Georgia, MMI ends TTD and triggers PPD based on impairment rating (O.C.G.A. § 34-9-263); catastrophic injuries get lifetime benefits (O.C.G.A. § 34-9-200.1). In South Carolina, MMI triggers PPD within the 500-week cap (S.C. Code § 42-9-10, § 42-9-30). Medical benefits continue after MMI in both states. Do not settle a PI case before reaching MMI — and challenge premature determinations.

faqs.question: What is maximum medical improvement (MMI)?
faqs.answer: MMI is the point when your treating physician determines that your condition has stabilized and is unlikely to improve significantly with further treatment. It does not mean you are fully healed — it means you have recovered as much as you are going to. Your doctor assigns an impairment rating at MMI that quantifies any permanent loss of function.

faqs.question: Who determines when I have reached MMI?
faqs.answer: Your treating physician makes the MMI determination. However, the workers' comp insurer or the opposing party's insurance company may request an Independent Medical Examination (IME) if they disagree. You have the right to challenge a premature MMI determination with your own medical evidence.

faqs.question: How does MMI affect my workers comp benefits in Georgia?
faqs.answer: In Georgia, reaching MMI typically ends temporary total disability (TTD) benefits and triggers a transition to permanent partial disability (PPD) benefits based on your impairment rating (O.C.G.A. § 34-9-263). For catastrophic injuries, lifetime benefits may continue under O.C.G.A. § 34-9-200.1. Medical benefits continue regardless of MMI.

faqs.question: How does MMI affect my workers comp benefits in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: In South Carolina, MMI similarly ends TTD and triggers PPD benefits based on impairment rating and loss of earning capacity (S.C. Code § 42-9-30). The 500-week overall benefit cap (S.C. Code § 42-9-10) continues to apply. Medical benefits for the work injury continue after MMI with no time limit.

faqs.question: Should I settle my personal injury case before reaching MMI?
faqs.answer: Generally no. Settling before MMI means you do not know the full extent of your injuries or future medical costs. You risk accepting far less than your claim is worth. The exception is catastrophic injuries with obvious permanent disability and low insurance policy limits, where early settlement may make strategic sense.

faqs.question: What can I do if the insurer declares MMI prematurely?
faqs.answer: You can (1) request a second opinion from an independent physician, (2) have your attorney challenge the determination through the workers' comp board or in court, (3) provide additional medical evidence showing you have not yet stabilized, or (4) request that the court appoint an independent medical examiner. Do not accept a premature MMI without legal advice.
